articles.title: Thermax shares crash 16% after firm expects weak quarters ahead after muted Q1 results
articles.content: Thermax shares dropped significantly after reporting an 86% profit decline. Revenue rose 7% year-on-year, but earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization fell. Order inflow increased 2%, and the total order book grew. The company cited higher input costs and weaker export sales impacting performance. Geopolitical issues and currency fluctuations also contributed to cost pressures.

articles.title: Global Market: China's factory activity contracts unexpectedly in July; metal, commodity stocks may stay under pressure
articles.content: China's manufacturing activity unexpectedly slipped into contraction during July. The official manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index fell below 50 for the first time. Non-manufacturing sectors also contracted, indicating broader economic slowdown. This data suggests policymakers may need to introduce additional stimulus measures. Weak factory data could impact global commodity and Indian metal stocks.

articles.title: Global Market: BOJ keeps rates unchanged, signals readiness for further hikes as yen remains under pressure
articles.content: The Bank of Japan maintained its key interest rate at 1% on Friday. This decision followed government intervention to support the weakening Japanese yen. The central bank signaled potential future rate increases if inflation risks intensify. Its economic growth forecast for fiscal 2026 was upgraded in a quarterly report. Underlying inflation may exceed the 2% target, suggesting further tightening is possible.

articles.title: BOJ keeps rates steady, signals further rate hikes
articles.content: The Bank of Japan maintained its interest rates at one percent on Friday.  This decision came after a two-day meeting concluded by the central bank.  One board member voted for a higher rate, seeking a 1.25 percent increase.  Governor Kazuo Ueda will explain the policy decision at a news conference.  The bank stressed its readiness to raise borrowing costs to manage inflation.
